subject: Integration readiness: SDK quickstart, gateway routing & local sample apps
messages:

Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + proposed pilot scope (Sagewell)

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. A short recap and proposed pilot scope so we all have alignment:

- Goal: validate Redwood inference for physician note summarization and clinical triage suggestions (throughput ~250 req/min peak, avg payload ~700 tokens).
- Success metrics: 95th percentile latency < 300ms for standard path, end-to-end throughput target, and embedding-based recall > 0.85 on sample prompts.
- Pilot components: hosted sandbox API access, local SDK sample apps (Python + TS) for integration testing, and an embeddings + reranker end-to-end demo using your de-identified transcript set.
- Timeline: tech sync next week, 2-week tech validation, then pilot SOW.

Next steps for Sagewell: confirm the sample dataset share, and confirm whether the pilot needs Private (VPC) or Hosted with IP allowlist.

I've attached an initial SOW draft and included Mina to run the technical onboarding + quickstart.

[Attachment: pilot-sow-draft.pdf (PDF, 72 KB)]

Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed pilot scope (Sagewell) — tech onboarding + SDK quickstart

Thanks Marissa — hi Beth, quick technical follow-up with exact steps we recommend to get the SDKs and local sample apps running so your engineers can start smoke tests immediately. I kept this focused and runnable with copy/paste commands.

1) Sandbox credentials / auth
- For the pilot we'll provision an API key scoped to the sandbox project. For production you can choose API keys or OAuth with your IdP; we support both.
- If you need Private (VPC) for pilot, please flag it now — provisioning adds ~2 business days.

2) Python quickstart (local)
- Create venv: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
- Install: pip install redwood-inference==1.8.0
- Env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-sandbox-xxx
- Test call (structured output + tool-call hint):
  from redwood import Client
  client = Client()
  resp = client.generate(model="redwood-mini", input="Summarize the note and call out actionable items", structured=True, tools=["ehr_lookup"])
  print(resp.structured)

Notes: structured=True returns JSON schema we use for downstream tool calling; see sample-apps/py/structured_demo.py in the zip.

3) TypeScript quickstart (local)
- Node 18+, run: npm init -y && npm install @redwood/inference@1.8.0
- Env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-sandbox-xxx
- Example request (node):
  import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
  const client = new Redwood()
  const out = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-mini', prompt: 'Classify urgency and return schema', structured: true })
  console.log(out)

4) Embeddings + reranker workflow
- Use redwood.embeddings.embedBatch(records) to generate vectors locally; store in your vector DB (we recommend Pinecone or PGVector for pilot).
- Reranker: call client.rerank(model='reranker-v1', query, candidates) — returns score + explanatory highlights.

5) Routing and fallbacks
- We support per-route policies: latency-first (hosted low-latency variants) or cost-first (smaller quantized variants). For pilot, we'll route by default to hosted low-latency.
- Auto-fallback will hit a compatible quantized variant if capacity spikes; we'll surface metrics in the console.

6) Local testing checklist (attached)
- confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY present
- run sample-apps smoke tests: pytest ./sample-apps/py/tests and npm test in /sample-apps/ts
- verify CORS/network rules if using browser-based samples

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart-checklist.pdf, sample-apps.zip

Operational asks for Sagewell IT:
- If using Hosted sandbox: whitelist these ranges: 52.18.0.0/16, 34.72.0.0/16 (we'll provide final list).
- If you need logs forwarded to your SIEM, we'll enable an audit sink (additional config).

Proposed tech sync: Thu 09 Dec 10:00 AM PT — I've included a cal link below. If that works we'll provision keys and sandbox today.

—Mina

- Data residency: for the pilot we'll use de-identified data but would like confirmation that hosted sandbox keeps data in us-west region only.
- Auth: API key for pilot is fine — for production we'll want SSO/OAuth.

2) Are there any size limits on embedding batch calls? We'll likely send batches of ~2k texts.

Thanks Beth — quick answers and next steps before our call:

- Residency: hosted sandbox will be provisioned in us-west for this pilot (we'll include that in the SOW and console config).
- Structured schema versioning: yes — you can pin schema_version in the generate call (schema_version='v1.0') and we'll guarantee backward compatibility for pinned versions during the pilot.
- Embedding batch size: recommended max batch ~2048 items for the sandbox; we'll accept larger but will advise chunking for reliability.

- Upload sample-apps.zip to shared Drive and send link -> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cSandboxExample

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.
